summary: Backend-only validation of the iteration-42 fix on GET /api/feuds/hype. Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_hype_feuds.py with 10 pytest cases against the live public URL (https://vote-ui-polish.preview.emergentagent.com) using MongoDB (test_database) as the source of truth for engagement scores. Result: 9 PASSED, 1 SKIPPED (no natural comment-only-zero-vote feud in DB; the Live-Update test synthesizes exactly this condition and PASSES). All eight functional requirements listed in the review request are satisfied: (1) no zero-engagement feud leaks in; (2) every voted 7-day feud (36 in DB) appears in the response; (3) ordering is monotonic non-increasing on the engagement score, with newer created_at winning ties; (4) inserting a comment on a zero-engagement feud immediately surfaces it on the next call; (5) no feud outside the 7-day window is returned; (6) anonymous callers get my_vote=null on every feud; (7) authenticated calls (chat_a@test.it) return 200 with my_vote populated on the correct docs.
critical_code_review_comments: list_hype_feuds (server.py:1193-1278): pre-slice window is now 1500 candidates. With 385 total feuds in DB this is comfortably safe; if the corpus grows past 1500 within a 7-day rolling window the primary sort must be pushed into the Mongo aggregation to guarantee correctness. Not a bug today, just a future scale note.

The sort tuple uses `d.get('created_at') or ''` as tiebreaker. Since datetime > str comparison would raise, this only works because all docs actually have `created_at` set. Consider making the fallback a datetime.min for defensive coding.

Response returns votes_a/votes_b as None when the caller has not voted (this is _attach_percentages behavior). The test report notes from the request confirm this is intentional; the frontend must not rely on those numeric fields for the HYPE rail unless my_vote is present.
seed_data_creation: None persistent. TestLiveUpdate inserts one synthetic comment (comment_id starts with 'cmt_TEST_HYPE_LIVE_') and deletes it in the finally block. Verified no residue post-run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend DB is 'test_database' (NOT 'populus'). At snapshot time DB had 385 feuds, 60 comments, 14 replies, 199 votes. 36 voted feuds in the last 7 days, all present in HYPE. 308 zero-vote feuds exist in the 7-day window and correctly EXCLUDED. The natural DB has zero comment-only-zero-vote feuds, so test_comment_only_feud_is_included legitimately skips; the Live-Update test covers that requirement synthetically. All tests read engagement directly from Mongo (via _db_engagement helper) so they don't depend on the API's response hiding votes_a/votes_b when revealed=False.
rca_of_issue: Iteration 41 sorted primarily by day (YYYY-MM-DD DESC) then engagement, so today's zero-engagement feuds outranked yesterday's voted ones, and no filter excluded score<=0 items. Iteration-42 fix (server.py:1241-1264) computes score = votes_a+votes_b+2*comments+replies via one $group per collection, hard-drops score<=0, and sorts by (score DESC, created_at DESC). Candidate window increased 400→1500 to prevent voted feuds being pre-sliced. Verified end-to-end with the live public URL: engagement scores match Mongo reality, ordering is monotonic on score, tie-breaks correctly follow created_at.
